judge.reason: It asserts an exact value for the set, which is a provable mathematical claim and is identical to e1.

options.counterfactual: Every normalized 2-quasitrace sends the successive differences of a bounded increasing positive sequence to zero, even when the sequence has no least upper bound.
options.approach: Investigate whether matrix amplification proves exhaustion: if positive elements have bounded partial sums, their quasitraces tend to zero. Apply this directly to a_{n+1}-a_n, without constructing a supremum.

options.counterfactual: Every normalized 2-quasitrace sends the successive differences of a bounded increasing positive sequence to zero, even when the sequence has no least upper bound.
options.approach: Assume a counterexample to exhaustion and pass to spectral projections of the successive differences. Seek an infinite-family argument excluding projections of uniformly positive quasitrace with bounded partial sums.

options.counterfactual: Every normalized 2-quasitrace sends the successive differences of a bounded increasing positive sequence to zero, even when the sequence has no least upper bound.
options.approach: Analyze the restriction of the quasitrace to the separable algebra generated by the sequence. Look for an exhaustion theorem whose hypotheses can be verified there without assuming global quasitrace linearity.

options.counterfactual: The finite AW*-factor hypotheses already guarantee that every bounded increasing self-adjoint sequence has a least upper bound in the ordinary self-adjoint order.
options.approach: Audit the exact hypotheses of monotone sequential completeness results for finite AW*-factors. Distinguish completeness in the ordinary order from completeness of the projection lattice and from spectral-order completeness.

options.counterfactual: The finite AW*-factor hypotheses already guarantee that every bounded increasing self-adjoint sequence has a least upper bound in the ordinary self-adjoint order.
options.approach: Revisit the compatible-graph construction and identify an additional property specific to finite AW*-factors that guarantees an everywhere-defined bounded graph in the original algebra. Then verify leastness against every self-adjoint upper bound.

options.counterfactual: The finite AW*-factor hypotheses already guarantee that every bounded increasing self-adjoint sequence has a least upper bound in the ordinary self-adjoint order.
options.approach: Investigate an affiliated-operator construction of the supremum. Determine whether boundedness forces the resulting affiliated operator to belong to the original factor, without assuming a von Neumann representation.

options.counterfactual: Failure of quasitrace linearity in a finite AW*-factor can be converted into a bounded increasing sequence with constant positive quasitrace increments and no least upper bound.
options.approach: Start from a positive additivity defect and investigate whether matrix amplification or passage to corners can reproduce it at arbitrarily many stages while keeping the total positive sum bounded.

options.counterfactual: Failure of quasitrace linearity in a finite AW*-factor can be converted into a bounded increasing sequence with constant positive quasitrace increments and no least upper bound.
options.approach: Study the supremum of sums of quasitrace values over finite positive families whose sum is at most one. Determine whether nonlinearity forces enough uniform divergence to construct an infinite constant-increment sequence.

options.counterfactual: Failure of quasitrace linearity in a finite AW*-factor can be converted into a bounded increasing sequence with constant positive quasitrace increments and no least upper bound.
options.approach: Investigate an ultrapower construction from increasingly long finite positive families. Check separately that constant increments survive and that the resulting sequence genuinely lacks a least upper bound.
